candidates.name: PostgreSQL full-text search

signals: The official PostgreSQL versions feed marks major 18 current and supported through 2030-11-14.
Full-text search is shipped in PostgreSQL, so it does not add a separately distributed search server.

rationale.text: PostgreSQL 18.4 and its built-in full-text search are available under the PostgreSQL License.
Using the same database for records and lexical indexing reduces P0 operational surface while preserving transaction and backup boundaries.
Chinese tokenization and ranking quality on real marketing documents has not been measured.

alternatives: OpenSearch behind a replaceable search adapter
candidates.fallback: Keep the deterministic lexical fallback for degraded-mode retrieval and fixture tests.
candidates.privateDeployment: Supported in the project Docker deployment; no hosted search service is required.

coreIntegration.boundary: Execute workspace, client, project, and visibility predicates in SQL before ranking; expose retrieval through a replaceable repository interface.

candidates.name: pgvector

signals: The official repository tag feed identifies v0.8.6 on 2026-07-29.
The repository LICENSE is the permissive PostgreSQL License.

rationale.text: pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension and can be deployed with the same private PostgreSQL service.
It is the narrowest current vector-index candidate and avoids a second database in M2.
Index choice, embedding model, recall, latency, memory, rebuild, deletion propagation, and Chinese retrieval quality remain unbenchmarked.

alternatives: Qdrant behind a vector-store adapter if measured scale or recall requires it
candidates.fallback: Disable semantic scoring and retain scoped PostgreSQL FTS plus deterministic lexical retrieval.
candidates.privateDeployment: Supported as an extension in the private PostgreSQL container; pin both image digest and extension version before M2 implementation.

coreIntegration.boundary: Application query builder must apply authorization predicates before vector distance ordering; embeddings and source versions remain application-owned.

candidates.name: Procrastinate

signals: The official repository publishes release 3.9.0 and remains unarchived.
The README documents PostgreSQL-backed retries, periodic tasks, and task locking while also requesting additional maintainers.

rationale.text: Procrastinate 3.9.0 is MIT-licensed and uses PostgreSQL as its task queue backend.
Using the existing PostgreSQL service avoids adding a broker to the first private-deployment topology.
Crash recovery, cancellation, orphan-lock handling, and PostgreSQL 18.4 compatibility have not yet passed MarketOps integration tests.

alternatives: Project-owned PostgreSQL job table and worker
Celery behind the same JobQueue adapter if a separate broker becomes justified
candidates.fallback: Keep business job state and replayable inputs outside queue-owned tables so the adapter can be replaced without changing project audit history.
candidates.privateDeployment: Run in the existing private PostgreSQL network; job payloads contain immutable artifact IDs and scope IDs rather than raw customer text.

coreIntegration.boundary: All queue calls pass through a MarketOps JobQueue interface; canonical task states, permissions, idempotency keys, and audit events remain application-owned.

candidates.name: Docling

signals: The official release feed identifies v2.118.1 on 2026-08-07.
The repository LICENSE is MIT.

rationale.text: Docling is locally runnable and MIT-licensed, so its top-level license does not conflict with this Apache-2.0 repository.
An isolated parser adapter can extend PDF and complex document coverage without assigning source storage, citation identity, or permissions to Docling.
Chinese PDF/DOCX fidelity, OCR behavior, stable coordinates, transitive model licenses, download size, CPU and memory are not yet validated.

candidates.fallback: Retain the validated Markdown, CSV, and basic DOCX parser and return explicit unsupported-format errors.
candidates.privateDeployment: Run inside a private parser worker with network egress disabled by default; model artifacts require a separate license and hash inventory.

coreIntegration.boundary: Run Docling only in an isolated parser Worker process with network egress disabled by default; the application owns source bytes, SHA-256 identity, authorization, citations, audit, and failure semantics.

candidates.name: LangGraph

signals: The official release feed was updated on 2026-08-07.
The repository publishes multiple independently versioned packages, so the repository latest-release redirect is not a safe pin for the core LangGraph package.

rationale.text: The repository is MIT-licensed and actively publishes package releases.
M1 deterministic scheduling, approvals, and audit do not yet require a general agent state-machine framework.
No measured workflow complexity or recovery requirement currently justifies its runtime and migration cost.

alternatives: Explicit application services and database state transitions
A small internal job runner with idempotency keys
candidates.fallback: Continue with deterministic services; re-evaluate only when a tested multi-step recovery scenario cannot be expressed clearly.
candidates.privateDeployment: Possible, but no deployment is approved at M0-05.

coreIntegration.boundary: If adopted later, it may orchestrate jobs but must not own permission decisions, canonical project state, or irreversible external actions.

candidates.name: Unstructured

signals: The official release feed identifies 0.25.2 on 2026-08-03.
The top-level repository license is Apache-2.0.

rationale.text: Its top-level license is compatible with this repository's Apache-2.0 license.
Selecting two broad parser stacks before a real corpus benchmark would add duplicate supply-chain and operational cost.
Partition strategy, optional extras, transitive licenses, local model downloads, and Chinese fidelity are not audited here.

candidates.fallback: Use the validated basic parser or compare against Docling on the same private benchmark corpus.
candidates.privateDeployment: Possible; optional extras and model downloads must be enumerated before enabling them.

coreIntegration.boundary: May only be introduced behind the same parser contract and source-hash/citation controls.

candidates.name: Sentence Transformers

signals: The official repository publishes v5.7.0 and is not archived.

rationale.text: The runtime code is Apache-2.0 licensed.
A replaceable embedding adapter can use this runtime after a model-specific benchmark.
No model weight, training-data statement, Chinese quality, or resource profile has been approved.

alternatives: A BYOK embedding API behind the same adapter
candidates.fallback: Use scoped lexical retrieval when no approved embedding implementation is configured.
candidates.privateDeployment: Possible only with separately pinned and licensed model weights.

coreIntegration.boundary: Evaluation candidate only; model artifacts and vectors remain versioned behind the Embedding Adapter.

candidates.name: FlagEmbedding

signals: The official repository publishes v1.4.0 and is not archived.

rationale.text: The runtime code is MIT licensed.
Its multilingual model entry points make it a relevant benchmark candidate for Chinese and mixed-language retrieval.
Upstream capability claims, model-weight licensing, retrieval quality, and resource use have not been independently validated.

alternatives: A BYOK embedding API behind the same adapter
candidates.fallback: Use scoped lexical retrieval when no approved embedding implementation is configured.
candidates.privateDeployment: Possible only after model weights, download hashes, offline behavior, and resource limits are approved.

coreIntegration.boundary: Evaluation candidate only; model artifacts and vectors remain versioned behind the Embedding Adapter.

candidates.name: OR-Tools

signals: The official repository publishes v9.15 and is not archived.

rationale.text: OR-Tools is Apache-2.0 licensed and provides constraint-solving capabilities.
The current deterministic finish-to-start schedule does not justify a general optimizer.
No observed user project has established a resource-leveling or optimization requirement.

candidates.fallback: Keep the M0-03 deterministic scheduling semantics and expose unsupported resource constraints explicitly.
candidates.privateDeployment: Possible, but no runtime is approved until a real optimization requirement and benchmark exist.

coreIntegration.boundary: Evaluation candidate only; formal schedule state and conflict explanations remain application-owned.

candidates.name: Apache Tika

signals: The official repository tag feed identifies 3.3.2 on 2026-07-21.
The repository LICENSE is Apache-2.0.

rationale.text: Apache Tika is Apache-2.0 licensed and can run as a local Java service.
Its separate JVM/service footprint is not justified before the chosen parser fails a measured format case.
Source-coordinate fidelity, table semantics, OCR configuration, and resource use on the target corpus are not measured.

candidates.fallback: Use it only as a quarantined fallback for formats not handled by the primary parser.
candidates.privateDeployment: Possible as a separate local process with explicit time, memory, file-size, and network limits.

coreIntegration.boundary: Any later adapter must preserve application-owned file hashes, coordinates, warnings, and explicit failure behavior.

candidates.name: Qdrant

signals: The official repository publishes v1.19.0 and is not archived.

rationale.text: Qdrant is Apache-2.0 licensed and provides filtered dense, sparse, and hybrid retrieval features.
A second database would add backup, restore, migration, and tenant-configuration cost before scale requires it.
No MarketOps benchmark shows PostgreSQL exact vector search is insufficient.

alternatives: Re-evaluate Qdrant behind a vector-store adapter after measured thresholds fail
candidates.fallback: Use scoped PostgreSQL retrieval and keep vector-store calls behind an application-owned adapter.
candidates.privateDeployment: Not included in P0 Docker topology; later evaluation must include backup, restore, deletion propagation, and isolation tests.

coreIntegration.boundary: No bundled service in P0; any future trial must preserve application-owned scope filtering and citation contracts.

candidates.name: Dify

signals: The official latest-release redirect resolves to 1.16.1.
The LICENSE adds a commercial-license trigger for multi-tenant operation and frontend logo/copyright restrictions to a modified Apache-2.0 base.

rationale.text: Dify's repository license is not plain Apache-2.0 and contains additional multi-tenant and frontend conditions.
Embedding or forking the platform would create avoidable licensing, branding, upgrade, and product-boundary risk.
A separately negotiated commercial license was not evaluated.

alternatives: Narrow MIT/Apache/PostgreSQL components behind project-owned interfaces
Use an external Dify deployment only through a user-configured API after separate terms review
candidates.fallback: Keep project state, RAG isolation, workflow approvals, and model adapters in the MarketOps application.
candidates.privateDeployment: Technically self-hostable, but not approved as a bundled or embedded dependency.

coreIntegration.boundary: No source embedding, fork, bundled container, or frontend reuse.

candidates.name: n8n

signals: The official latest-release redirect resolves to n8n@2.33.7.
The repository distinguishes Sustainable Use licensed files from separately licensed enterprise files.

rationale.text: The Sustainable Use License limits use and distribution and is not Apache-2.0.
Bundling n8n as the workbench's automation engine would conflict with the desired independently redistributable Apache-2.0 core.
Commercial enterprise terms were not requested or evaluated.

alternatives: Optional user-operated n8n connector over an API after separate license review
candidates.fallback: Implement only the small number of deterministic M1 jobs and external-action approvals required by the product.
candidates.privateDeployment: Self-hostable under its terms, but not approved for bundling or core redistribution.

coreIntegration.boundary: No bundled runtime or copied nodes; a future connector must be optional and independently configured.

candidates.name: MinIO Community Edition

signals: GitHub states that the repository was archived on 2026-04-25 and is read-only.
The repository README states that it is no longer maintained and community edition is source-only.
The repository LICENSE is AGPL-3.0.

rationale.text: The repository is archived, unmaintained, and AGPL-3.0 licensed.
Bundling it would add both maintenance and network-copyleft review risk without being required for the first single-user deployment.
The successor AIStor license and commercial terms were not evaluated.

alternatives: Local filesystem storage behind an object-store interface
Apache-2.0 licensed SeaweedFS after a separate audit
candidates.fallback: Store source files on a private local volume with hashes, backup documentation, and a replaceable object-store interface.
candidates.privateDeployment: Do not bundle the archived community server; permit user-supplied S3-compatible endpoints later.

coreIntegration.boundary: Depend only on a narrow object-storage interface, never MinIO-specific behavior.

candidates.name: RSSHub

signals: The official repository LICENSE is AGPL-3.0.
No stable release pin was established from the official releases page during this audit.

rationale.text: RSSHub is AGPL-3.0 licensed.
Bundling or modifying it for M3 source ingestion would require avoidable AGPL compliance analysis and would couple the product to a broad route ecosystem.
A future separately operated, unmodified RSSHub service and its precise network boundary were not evaluated.

alternatives: Direct RSS/Atom reader using standard protocols
User-configured external RSSHub endpoint after separate terms review
candidates.fallback: M3 begins with user-approved RSS/Atom URLs and official APIs through narrow source adapters.
candidates.privateDeployment: Not approved as a bundled service; an independently operated endpoint may be considered later.

coreIntegration.boundary: No bundled code or copied routes; source adapters consume standard feed output only.
